name: Los Alamos National Laboratory, LANSCE (Technical Area 53)
notes: Overpass (overpass-api.de and lz4.overpass-api.de) refused essentially every connection attempt for LANL/ORNL after the SLAC extract succeeded (TCP connection refused, then HTTP 429, then connection refused again); overpass.kumi.systems and overpass.osm.ch both answered but returned zero elements even for known-good queries and were dropped as likely partial/regional mirrors. maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass/api/interpreter, suggested mid-session, did return real, complete data: a 1,817-element extract of the wider Los Alamos townsite (streets, apartments, generic industrial buildings, none named or tagged in any way suggesting LANSCE), and a tight 700 m box directly around the LANSCE node itself came back with zero building ways. TA-53's accelerator/experimental core is therefore genuinely almost unmapped in OpenStreetMap, not merely unreached this session. Nominatim's /search and /lookup endpoints were reachable throughout and are the source of the one point drawn on this map.

TA-53 is a security-sensitive area of Los Alamos National Laboratory: per the research brief, only accelerator/experimental areas shown on public LANSCE maps may be depicted, never fences or gates. No fence, gate or access-control feature is drawn or was found.
TA-53 is security-sensitive; only the public technical-area line and named accelerator and experimental-area buildings from a county map service are drawn, no gates or fences.

Release pass (2026-10-25): the earlier worklog's finding that TA-53 was 'almost unmapped in OpenStreetMap' came from searching around OSM node 8041862150 'LANSCE', which is the WEST end of TA-53, 2.8 km from the LANSCE building cluster. An OSM API extract of the cluster (2026-10-25) holds 118 TA-53 features, many tagged with the LANL building number in `ref` (53-0003, 53-0007, 53-0017, 53-0030, 53-0364, 53-0365 ...), and Los Alamos County publishes a TA-53 boundary and building footprints with the same numbers (the OSM and county outlines of buildings 6, 14, 17, 18, 19, 365 agree to 1-9 m).

The old marker geometry:lansce-site-marker (OSM point at the western tip of TA-53, tied to site:lanl-lansce, whose only timeline is LSND's 1993-98 placement, so it vanished in 2026) is retired. The linac structure carries accelerator:lansce (active since 1972); the other features have no entity and no `valid` (timeless) and carry site_id site:lanl-lansce.

Building 53-3 is drawn from two sources: the long wing from OSM (linac, ODbL) and the main hall from the county layer. OSM building 53-0007 (WNR, 22 m across) and the county's 'Weapons Neutron Research Build' (BLDG_ID 7, 205 m long, thin) are different outlines of the same number; the county outline is drawn.
TA-53 is security-sensitive; only the public technical-area line and named accelerator and experimental-area buildings are drawn, no gates or fences.

summary.plain: The LANSCE accelerator site (Technical Area 53, the Meson Physics Facility) at Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico: the 695 m building along the mesa top that houses the 800 MeV proton linac, the main hall, the Proton Storage Ring building (a 32 m circle) and the Lujan Center, with the technical-area boundary and the other buildings. Positions come from OpenStreetMap and Los Alamos County map data, not from a survey.
summary.technical: Local map for facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory. geometry:lansce-linac-building is OSM way 370719333 (ref 53-0003, 695 m x 26 m, east-west) as the linac structure (accelerator:lansce); county 'Structures' footprints (BLDG_ID, DESC_) give the main hall, the Proton Storage Ring facility (span 31.8 m vs the 30 m diameter in LA-UR-05-9402), the Lujan Center, WNR, a 'Gta Facility', a neutrino-experiment service building and 70 others; the county TA-53 polygon is the boundary. detector:lsnd is unlocated. OSM and county outlines of the same building numbers agree to a few metres.

unlocated.backlog: Find a LANSCE/LAMPF-era civil-engineering drawing or the original LSND proposal's site plan giving Line A's/Area A's beamline heading and the A6 beam stop's coordinates or its distance and bearing from a surveyed LANSCE control point.
unlocated.reason: LSND's own NIM paper places it about 30 m from the A6 proton beam stop (src:lsnd-nim-1997-detector-paper), and a separate 2020 paper on LANSCE's Area A places a (different, later-proposed) target 'near the center of Area A, some 100 m downstream of the end of the 800-MeV accelerator' (src:geo-lanl-fpns-area-a-nim-2020) -- but the 800-MeV accelerator's own end point is not itself located this session (see accelerator:lansce, above), and no source gives the switchyard/Line-A bend's heading, so a derived point would rest on an unsourced direction, not a sourced one. LSND is therefore left undrawn rather than guessed; the detector-hosting site itself (site:lanl-lansce) is drawn. Release pass 2026-10-25: the county layer has a 'Neutrion Exper Service Bl' (building 364, drawn as a context building) at LANSCE, but nothing fetched says it belongs to LSND or where the A6 beam stop is, so LSND is still not placed.
